standards.name: RootSystemML (RSML)
standards.abstract: RSML (RootSystemML) is an XML-based file format for representing plant root system architecture (RSA) data derived from 2D or 3D images. It encodes image metadata, scene/plant/root topology and geometry (polylines of points), continuous functions along root paths (e.g. diameter samples), annotations at scene/plant/root scales, and optional time-sequence information. The specification (RootSystemML project) is presented on the RootSystemML website and GitHub and is accompanied by an XSD validator and conversion/analysis tools (R, Python, ImageJ, Excel, C#). The standard addresses portability and interoperability of root architecture data across analysis, modelling and visualization tools and provides a thesaurus of recommended property and function names and their types.

classification.rationale: The RSML documentation defines concrete XML elements and named fields with explicit types (e.g. <version>, <unit>, <image><name>, <property-definition><type>, thesaurus entries with stated types like 'string', 'integer', 'real', 'boolean', and enumerated possible values). This is genuine field-level structure rather than prose guidance, so the source is best represented as a MetadataTable.

metadata.version.name: metadata.version
metadata.version.descr: Format version identifier for the RSML file

metadata.unit.name: metadata.unit
metadata.unit.descr: Unit of measurement used for geometry and values (e.g. pixel, mm)
metadata.unit.evidence: The unit tag specifies what units the resolution tag converts to, with the resolution tag detailing the conversion rate between pixels and the unit. ... All geometry and values within the document use the pixel as the unit of measurement, with the assumption that they refer directly to some underlying [image data].

raw_full_info.units_list: pixel, m/metre, cm/centimetre, mm/millimetre, um/micrometre, nm/nanometre

metadata.resolution.name: metadata.resolution
metadata.resolution.descr: Conversion rate between pixels and the stated unit (numeric)

metadata.last-modified.name: metadata.last-modified
metadata.last-modified.descr: Date and time stamp of the last modification of the RSML file (ISO8601)
metadata.last-modified.evidence:
- date and time stamp of the last modification of the rsml file
  - It should respect the [ISO8601][] format

metadata.software.name: metadata.software
metadata.software.descr: Name of software that produced or edited the RSML file

metadata.user.name: metadata.user
metadata.user.descr: User identifier (author/editor) recorded in the RSML file

metadata.file-key.name: metadata.file-key
metadata.file-key.descr: User-provided textual representation or identifier for the file (recommended unique identifier)
metadata.file-key.evidence: - File-key provides a position for a text representation of this file. Use of this field is left to the user’s discretion, we recommend it is used as a unique identifier.

metadata.image.name.name: metadata.image.name
metadata.image.name.descr: Filename or path of the image used to construct the root system (mandatory)
metadata.image.name.evidence: - **name** (mandatory) specifies the file name of the image used to construct this root system. The name can be an absolute or relative url, or simply a file

metadata.image.captured.name: metadata.image.captured
metadata.image.captured.descr: Date/time when the source image was captured (ISO8601)
metadata.image.captured.evidence: - **captured** (optional) is a dateTime value indicating the original time of capture for that image. It should be given in  [ISO8601][] format

metadata.image.sha256.name: metadata.image.sha256
metadata.image.sha256.descr: SHA-256 hash of the entire image file (optional), used to fingerprint the image
metadata.image.sha256.evidence: - **sha256** (optional) specifies the hash of the entire image file using the [SHA-256][] hashing algorithm. This file fingerprint represents a more reliable means to locate the original source image

metadata.time-sequence.label.name: metadata.time-sequence.label
metadata.time-sequence.label.descr: Label identifying a time-sequence group (used when RSML files belong to a series)

metadata.time-sequence.index.name: metadata.time-sequence.index
metadata.time-sequence.index.descr: Index identifying the position in the time sequence (integer, ascending order)
metadata.time-sequence.index.evidence: - **index** identifies the position in the sequence relative to all other images with that label. Indexes should be unique within a sequence, and in ascending order relative to time captured.

metadata.time-sequence.unified.name: metadata.time-sequence.unified
metadata.time-sequence.unified.descr: Boolean indicating whether IDs are shared across files in the time sequence
metadata.time-sequence.unified.evidence: - **unified** (optional) is a Boolean value indicating whether corresponding plant and root components share the same ids across files in the time sequence. ... the default value of false is assigned.

metadata.property-definition.name: metadata.property-definition
metadata.property-definition.descr: Definition of properties/functions used in the scene: label and type (type chosen from standard units/variable types)
metadata.property-definition.type: object (label: string, type: enum [boolean, integer, real, string])
metadata.property-definition.evidence:
<property-definitions>
      <property-definition>
        <label>parent-node</label>
        <type>integer</type>
      </property-definition>
    </property-definitions>

  ...

  - It allows a given file to define the names and types of [properties][], using the **property-definition** subelement, and of [functions][], using the **function-definition** subelement, that are used in the [scene][].

scene.plant.id.name: scene.plant.id
scene.plant.id.descr: Plant identifier (id attribute on plant element)

scene.plant.label.name: scene.plant.label
scene.plant.label.evidence: - Two pre-defined attributes of label and ID exist that should be understood by all software. The label is the semantic name given to a specific root in some software, the ID represents a unique identifier for that root or plant.

scene.root.id.name: scene.root.id
scene.root.id.descr: Root identifier (id attribute on root element)

scene.root.po:accession.name: scene.root.po:accession
scene.root.po:accession.descr: Plant Ontology accession (po:accession attribute) linking root categories to PO terms
scene.root.po:accession.evidence: - The po:accession attribute links to the plant ontology. They are expected to be of the form PO:XXXXXXX where X represents a single digit.

scene.geometry.polyline.point.x.name: scene.geometry.polyline.point.x
scene.geometry.polyline.point.x.descr: X coordinate of a polyline point (image domain)
scene.geometry.polyline.point.x.evidence: - Being defined in the image domain, each point on the polyline contains mandatory x and y values, and an optional z value for 3D data.

scene.geometry.polyline.point.y.name: scene.geometry.polyline.point.y
scene.geometry.polyline.point.y.descr: Y coordinate of a polyline point (image domain)
scene.geometry.polyline.point.y.evidence: - Being defined in the image domain, each point on the polyline contains mandatory x and y values, and an optional z value for 3D data.

scene.geometry.polyline.point.z.name: scene.geometry.polyline.point.z
scene.geometry.polyline.point.z.descr: Optional Z coordinate for 3D polyline points (image domain)
scene.geometry.polyline.point.z.evidence: - Being defined in the image domain, each point on the polyline contains mandatory x and y values, and an optional z value for 3D data.

scene.functions.function.name.name: scene.functions.function.name
scene.functions.function.name.descr: Function name attached to a root (e.g. diameter)

scene.functions.function.domain.name: scene.functions.function.domain
scene.functions.function.domain.descr: Domain over which function samples are defined (polyline, uniform, length)
scene.functions.function.domain.evidence:
- There are three domains in which a function can be defined, these all directly map to the polyline geometry:
  - The ‘polyline’ domain defines a series of discrete samples along the length of a root.
  - The ‘uniform’ domain represents a series of uniformly distributed samples along the length of a root... 
  - The ‘length’ domain represents samples at specific length positions along a root, again on the polyline.

scene.functions.function.sample.name: scene.functions.function.sample
scene.functions.function.sample.descr: One sample value of a function (numeric real)

scene.annotations.annotation.name.name: scene.annotations.annotation.name
scene.annotations.annotation.name.evidence: - Annotations contain one pixel position representing the position of the value, and the value containing the actual annotation. Optional additional points can be added by software to represent a polygon to which the annotation applies.

scene.annotations.annotation.point.name: scene.annotations.annotation.point
scene.annotations.annotation.point.descr: Point(s) representing position(s) of an annotation (x,y,(z) coordinates)
scene.annotations.annotation.point.type: object (x: real, y: real, z: real optional)
scene.annotations.annotation.point.evidence:
<annotation name="Annotated length">
    <point x="334.41904" y="289.77496" />
    <point x="361.12778" y="360.91653" />
    <value>Interesting section</value>
    <software>RootNav</software>
  </annotation>

thesaurus.species.name: thesaurus.species
thesaurus.species.descr: Species property (scene, plant) - prefer Latin names
thesaurus.species.evidence:
###### species: (scene,plant)
Indicate the plant species in the image. Prefer latin names. ([type][]: string)

thesaurus.genotype.name: thesaurus.genotype
thesaurus.genotype.evidence:
###### genotype: (scene,plant)
Indicate the plant genotype in the image. ([type][]: string)

thesaurus.medium.name: thesaurus.medium
thesaurus.medium.evidence:
###### medium: (scene)
Indicate the growing medium used for the plant present in the image. ([type][]: string)

thesaurus.treatment.name: thesaurus.treatment
thesaurus.treatment.evidence:
###### treatment: (scene)
Indicate wether a specific treatment was applied to the plants. ([type][]: string)

thesaurus.age_of_plant.name: thesaurus.age_of_plant
thesaurus.age_of_plant.descr: Age of the plant in days (scene, plant)
thesaurus.age_of_plant.evidence:
###### age_of_plant: (scene, plant)
Age of the plant, in days. ([type][]: integer)

thesaurus.complete.name: thesaurus.complete
thesaurus.complete.descr: Indicates if the root axis has been fully traced (root-level property)
thesaurus.complete.evidence:
###### complete: (root)
Indicates if the root axes has been fully traced ([type][]: string)

 - “yes”: it is fully traced (from parent to tip)
 - “no”: only a part of the axes has been traced

thesaurus.branch-list.name: thesaurus.branch-list
thesaurus.branch-list.descr: Indicates which sub-axes have been traced (root-level property)
thesaurus.branch-list.evidence:
###### branch-list: (root)
Indicates which sub-axes have been traced ([type][]: string)

 - “complete”: root children branch have all been traced
 - “validated”: complete and it has been validated by the user
 - “random”: a random sample has been traced
 - “stratified”: a selected sample, representative of the roots type and density, has been traced

thesaurus.parent-node.name: thesaurus.parent-node
thesaurus.parent-node.descr: Connects a root axis to its parent axis by indicating the parent node index (root-level integer)
thesaurus.parent-node.evidence:
###### parent-node: (root)
This property allows **to connect** the root axes to the parent axes. More precisely, it indicates which node of the parent axe is actually the first node of this axe. ([type][]: integer)

 - Eg: “3” means this axe 1st node is the same as the 3rd node of parent axe

thesaurus.parent-position.name: thesaurus.parent-position
thesaurus.parent-position.descr: Measured position on parent axis where branch starts (real)
thesaurus.parent-position.evidence:
###### parent-position: (root)
Indicates at which position on the parent axe this axe starts. This preperty is to indicates a measured branching position along the parent root. It does not connect the axes. ([type][]: real)

 - Eg: "3.2" means 20% between the 3rd and 4th nodes in parent polyline

thesaurus.user-confidence.name: thesaurus.user-confidence
thesaurus.user-confidence.descr: User-provided confidence in measured polyline (scene, plant, root)
thesaurus.user-confidence.evidence:
###### user-confidence: (scene, plant and root)
Indicates the confidence on the measured axe polyline given by user ([type][]: string)

 - high
 - medium
 - low
 - invalid

thesaurus.software-confidence.name: thesaurus.software-confidence
thesaurus.software-confidence.descr: Software-provided confidence in tracing (real between 0 and 1)
thesaurus.software-confidence.evidence:
###### software-confidence: (scene, plant or root)
Indicates the confidence on the measured axe polyline given by (automated) software ([type][]: real)

 - A value in [0,1]: trust in the tracing, 1 been highest trust

thesaurus.function.diameter.name: thesaurus.function.diameter
thesaurus.function.diameter.descr: Function recording diameter at nodes of the root polyline (units: pixel), type real
thesaurus.function.diameter.evidence:
###### diameter:
This gives the recorded diameter at each node of the root polyline in pixel. ([type][]: real)

 - Positive values \[0,inf)

thesaurus.function.confidence.name: thesaurus.function.confidence
thesaurus.function.confidence.descr: Function representing confidence in node positions (real in [0,1])
thesaurus.function.confidence.evidence:
###### confidence:
confidence in the root node position of the polyline ([type][]: real)

 - A value in [0,1]: trust in the node postion, 1 been highest trust

thesaurus.function.xxx-confidence.name: thesaurus.function.xxx-confidence
thesaurus.function.xxx-confidence.descr: Generic pattern for a function giving confidence in another property (real in [0,1])
thesaurus.function.xxx-confidence.evidence:
###### xxxx-confidence:
confidence in the root property `xxxx` ([type][]: real)

 - A value in [0,1]: trust in the property value, 1 been highest trust

standards.notes: Extracted fields reflect explicit XML element names and the RSML thesaurus entries and type guidance provided on the RootSystemML website and example files.
